standard.title: Drums, Large, Fixed Ends — Specification (Part 1: Grade A Drums; Part 2: Grade B Drums) (Fourth Revision)
standard.description: This standard specifies the physical dimensions, material properties, constructional details, and rigorous performance testing requirements (including drop, leak, and hydraulic pressure tests) for large, fixed-end steel drums of 200-litre nominal capacity. These containers are intended for the secure packaging, storage, and transport of liquids, semi-liquids, bulk chemicals, and industrial raw materials.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Drums and Tins (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all Large Fixed-End Steel Drums (Grade A and Grade B) must conform to IS 1783 (Part 1 and Part 2) and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified drums in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Exemption is granted solely for export-oriented shipments and pre-filled imported containers. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial steel packaging.
requirements: Every certified fixed-end steel drum must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 1783 Part 1 or Part 2) stenciled on the drum body or ends.
The nominal capacity must be 200 Litres, and the minimum gross capacity must be at least 210 Litres when measured with water at ambient temperature.

Grade A drums are heavy-duty containers constructed from cold-reduced steel sheets of nominal thickness 1.25 mm for both the cylindrical body and end plates. Ends must be double-seamed (Type 1) or spiral/triple-seamed (Type 2) to ensure maximum mechanical strength.

Grade B drums are standard-duty containers. Type 1 utilized 1.25 mm nominal sheet thickness for both the body and ends with double-seamed end seams. Type 2 utilizes slightly thinner steel sheets of 1.00 mm nominal thickness with spiral or triple-seamed ends.
The longitudinal body seam must be continuously resistance welded to provide a completely air-tight and robust joint.

Every single drum must be tested for leak-tightness before dispatch. The drum must withstand an internal air pressure of 0.3 kg/cm² to 0.5 kg/cm² (depending on grade/type) while submerged in water or sprayed with a soap solution, showing zero bubbles, leaks, or structural sweating.

To guarantee structural safety during rough handling or transportation accidents, the drum is filled with water to 98 percent of its gross capacity and dropped from a specified height (e.g. 1.2 meters) onto a solid concrete or steel pad. It must show zero splits, structural tears, or leakage.

The drum must withstand a high internal hydrostatic pressure (e.g., 1.5 to 2.0 kg/cm² or 150-200 kPa for Grade A) for a minimum of 5 minutes without showing any signs of leakage, sweating, seam slippage, or permanent warping.

The interior of each drum must be completely clean, dry, and free from scale, rust, or foreign matter. If the raw steel sheet is incompatible with the product to be filled, a suitable protective lining, lacquer, or epoxy coating must be applied.

A lot comprises up to 300 drums (or 1,000 kg, whichever is greater) of the same grade, size, and condition. Random samples are selected for visual, dimensional, and destructive physical testing. Non-conforming defectives must stay within strictly bounded acceptance limits, or the entire lot is rejected.
